directAnswer: Pope Benedict IV was a Roman priest who reigned from 900 to 903. He crowned Louis of Provence emperor in 901 and excommunicated the murderers of Archbishop Fulk of Reims. Later writers praised his generosity, but the record of his pontificate is slight, and even the exact end date is uncertain.

sections.h2: A Formosan Priest Who Became Pope
paras: Benedict was a Roman, the son of a man named Mammolus, and had been ordained priest by Formosus. His election in early 900 thus signaled the continuing dominance of the party that had restored Formosus's memory. The tenth-century historian Flodoard of Reims commended him for his kindness to the poor and his concern for the common good.
In 900 he excommunicated the men who had murdered Fulk, archbishop of Reims, a crime connected to the feuds of the Flemish count Baldwin II.

sections.h2: The Coronation of Louis of Provence
paras: After the death of Lambert of Spoleto, Italy lacked an emperor. Louis of Provence, a grandson of Emperor Louis II through his mother, came south and was crowned emperor by Benedict in Rome in 901. His rule proved short-lived; in 905 his rival Berengar captured and blinded him, which is why he is remembered as Louis the Blind.
Benedict died in the summer of 903 and was buried in St. Peter's. Beyond these few events, little survives about him.

keyFacts: Roman, son of Mammolus; ordained priest by Formosus
Excommunicated the murderers of Archbishop Fulk of Reims (900)
Crowned Louis of Provence emperor in 901
Praised by Flodoard of Reims for his charity

faqs.question: Which emperor did Benedict IV crown?
faqs.answer: Louis of Provence, in 901. Louis was later blinded by his rival Berengar and is known as Louis the Blind.

faqs.question: Why is Benedict IV well regarded despite the period's turmoil?
faqs.answer: The chronicler Flodoard of Reims praised his generosity to the poor and his devotion to the public good, though few details of his reign survive.
